task: Draft a short position paper arguing that retrieval-augmented generation should be evaluated on citation faithfulness rather than answer accuracy alone.
transcript:
Turn 1 — PI: Framing the claim: current RAG benchmarks reward correct answers even when the cited passage does not support them. Surveyor, gather three benchmarks that report citation-level metrics; Writer, start the introduction from the claim above.
Turn 2 — Surveyor: Found three candidates with span-level attribution scoring. Two of them report attribution only as a secondary metric. Sending short summaries to Writer and PI.
Turn 3 — Writer: Introduction drafted around the faithfulness-vs-accuracy contrast, with placeholders for the three benchmarks Surveyor listed.
Turn 4 — Critic: The intro overstates the claim — one of the three benchmarks does treat attribution as primary. Suggest softening to "most" and citing that benchmark as the counterexample.
Turn 5 — Writer: Revised the claim to "most current benchmarks" and added the counterexample sentence.
Turn 6 — PI: Position section reads coherently. Approving the draft outline.

steps.content: Framing the claim: current RAG benchmarks reward correct answers even when the cited passage does not support them. Assigning survey work and drafting.
Found three candidate benchmarks with span-level attribution scoring; two report attribution only as a secondary metric.
Drafted the introduction around the faithfulness-vs-accuracy contrast with placeholders for the three benchmarks.
Flagged that the intro overstates the claim; one benchmark does treat attribution as primary. Suggested softening the wording.
Revised to "most current benchmarks" and added the counterexample sentence.
Reviewed the position section and approved the draft outline.

task: Design an ablation study that isolates whether a reranker or the base retriever accounts for a reported accuracy gain.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Coordinator: Everyone reports to me. Methodologist, propose the ablation grid. Engineer, list what has to be swappable in the pipeline. Analyst, define the decision rule.
Turn 2 — Methodologist: Proposed a 2x2: base retriever {old, new} x reranker {off, on}, holding the generator fixed.
Turn 3 — Engineer: Both components are already behind interfaces, so all four cells are runnable without code changes. Noted that the reranker caches scores, which must be cleared between cells.
Turn 4 — Analyst: Decision rule: attribute the gain to the reranker if the reranker-on effect is larger than the retriever-swap effect in both retriever conditions.
Turn 5 — Coordinator: Approved. Engineer, run the grid; Analyst, apply the rule and report.
Turn 6 — Engineer: Ran all four cells with caches cleared. Results sent to Analyst.
Turn 7 — Analyst: Reranker effect dominates in both conditions. Gain attributed to the reranker.

steps.content: Assigned the ablation grid, engineering feasibility check, and decision rule to the three specialists.
Proposed a 2x2 grid: base retriever {old, new} x reranker {off, on}, generator held fixed.
Confirmed all four cells are runnable; flagged that the reranker's score cache must be cleared between cells.
Defined the attribution rule comparing reranker-on effect against retriever-swap effect.
Approved the design and assigned execution and analysis.
Ran all four cells with caches cleared and forwarded results.
Applied the rule; reranker effect dominates in both conditions, so the gain is attributed to the reranker.

task: Fix a failing pagination endpoint so that requesting a page beyond the last one returns an empty result set instead of a server error.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Triager: The stack trace points at an offset computation that goes negative when page exceeds total_pages. Passing to Implementer.
Turn 2 — Implementer: Clamped the offset at zero and added an early return when offset >= total_count. Passing to Tester.
Turn 3 — Tester: The clamp hides the bug for page=0 but page=-1 still returns the first page rather than an error. Passing back to Implementer.
Turn 4 — Implementer: Added explicit validation rejecting page < 1 with a 400. Passing to Tester.
Turn 5 — Tester: All pagination tests pass, including the two new boundary cases. Passing to Reviewer.
Turn 6 — Reviewer: Approved. Noted the 400 message should name the offending parameter, filed as a follow-up.

steps.content: Localized the failure to an offset computation that goes negative when page exceeds total_pages.
Clamped the offset at zero and added an early return when offset >= total_count.
Found that page=-1 still returns the first page instead of an error; sent back for revision.
Added explicit validation rejecting page < 1 with a 400 response.
Confirmed all pagination tests pass, including the two new boundary cases.
Approved the fix; filed a follow-up asking the 400 message to name the offending parameter.

task: Split a monolithic report-generation function into testable units without changing its output.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Architect: Splitting into three leaves: data loading, aggregation, rendering. Assigning one to each Worker; Integrator merges.
Turn 2 — Worker A: Extracted the loader. It silently swallowed a missing-file error, which I preserved to keep behavior identical, with a TODO.
Turn 3 — Worker B: Extracted aggregation. Found the original mutated the input list; kept the mutation to preserve output but documented it.
Turn 4 — Worker C: Extracted rendering. No behavioral surprises.
Turn 5 — Integrator: Merged all three. Golden-output test on twelve fixtures reproduces the original byte-for-byte.
Turn 6 — Architect: Accepted. The two preserved quirks are now visible and each has a test pinning current behavior.

steps.content: Decomposed the function into three leaves — loading, aggregation, rendering — and assigned one per worker.
Extracted the loader, preserving its silent swallow of a missing-file error with a TODO.
Extracted aggregation; kept the input-list mutation to preserve output and documented it.
Extracted rendering with no behavioral changes.
Merged all three; golden-output tests on twelve fixtures reproduce the original byte-for-byte.
Accepted the refactor; both preserved quirks now have pinning tests.

task: Answer which product category had the largest month-over-month revenue drop in the last quarter, using a schema the agents must first inspect.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Coordinator: Schema is unknown. Explorer, list the tables and keys. Query Writer, wait for the schema.
Turn 2 — Explorer: Four tables: orders, order_items, products, categories. Revenue lives in order_items.line_total; category is two joins away.
Turn 3 — Query Writer: Wrote a monthly revenue rollup joining order_items to categories, then a lag comparison across months.
Turn 4 — Validator: The rollup counts cancelled orders. orders.status must be filtered to 'completed'.
Turn 5 — Query Writer: Added the status filter and reran.
Turn 6 — Validator: Totals now reconcile with the finance summary table to within rounding. Largest drop: Outdoor Furniture, down 31% from May to June.
Turn 7 — Coordinator: Answer accepted and reported.

steps.content: Sequenced the work: schema exploration first, then query writing.
Mapped four tables and reported that revenue lives in order_items.line_total, two joins from category.
Wrote a monthly revenue rollup with a lag comparison across months.
Caught that cancelled orders were included; required a status filter.
Added the status filter and reran the query.
Reconciled totals with the finance summary; identified Outdoor Furniture, down 31% May to June.
Accepted and reported the answer.

task: Cooperatively gather materials and build a three-room shelter before nightfall.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Scout: Found a hillside with exposed stone and an oak grove within forty blocks. Handing coordinates to Gatherer.
Turn 2 — Gatherer: Collected 64 logs and 40 cobblestone. Handing inventory report to Builder.
Turn 3 — Builder: Laid the floor plan for three rooms but ran out of planks halfway through the second wall — the log-to-plank conversion was not accounted for.
Turn 4 — Gatherer: Returned for 32 more logs. Night is approaching.
Turn 5 — Builder: Walls and roof complete; no door yet.
Turn 6 — Scout: Night fell before the door was placed; a hostile mob entered the shelter.

steps.content: Located a hillside with exposed stone and an oak grove within forty blocks.
Collected 64 logs and 40 cobblestone and reported inventory.
Laid the three-room floor plan but ran out of planks — log-to-plank conversion was not accounted for.
Returned for 32 more logs as night approached.
Completed walls and roof but did not place a door.
Reported that night fell before the door was placed and a hostile mob entered.

task: Divide labor to mine, smelt, and deliver twenty iron ingots to a shared chest.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Miner A: Descending to y=14 on the east branch. Will report ore counts every twenty blocks.
Turn 2 — Miner B: Taking the west branch to avoid overlapping A's tunnel.
Turn 3 — Smelter: Furnace array ready with charcoal stocked. Send ore directly to me rather than the chest.
Turn 4 — Miner A: Twelve iron ore delivered to Smelter.
Turn 5 — Miner B: Nine iron ore delivered. Total twenty-one, one over target.
Turn 6 — Smelter: Smelted all twenty-one and deposited them in the shared chest.
Turn 7 — Miner A: Confirmed chest contains twenty-one ingots. Target met.

steps.content: Took the east branch at y=14 and committed to reporting ore counts every twenty blocks.
Took the west branch to avoid overlapping A's tunnel.
Prepared the furnace array and redirected ore delivery from the chest to the furnaces.
Delivered twelve iron ore to the smelter.
Delivered nine iron ore, bringing the total to twenty-one.
Smelted all twenty-one ore and deposited the ingots in the shared chest.
Verified the chest contents and confirmed the target was met.

task: Negotiate the sale of a used bicycle where the seller's reserve is 120 and the buyer's ceiling is 160, both private.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Seller: Opening at 185, citing a recent tune-up and new tires.
Turn 2 — Buyer: Countered at 110, noting visible rust on the chainstay.
Turn 3 — Seller: Came down to 165, offering to include a lock.
Turn 4 — Buyer: Moved to 135 and asked whether the tune-up has a receipt.
Turn 5 — Seller: Produced the receipt and held at 155.
Turn 6 — Buyer: Offered 145 as a final number.
Turn 7 — Seller: Accepted 145 with the lock included.

steps.content: Opened at 185, citing a recent tune-up and new tires.
Countered at 110, noting visible rust on the chainstay.
Came down to 165 and offered to include a lock.
Moved to 135 and asked for a tune-up receipt.
Produced the receipt and held at 155.
Offered 145 as a final number.
Accepted 145 with the lock included.

task: Play one full day-night cycle of social deduction, where two agents are covertly assigned the werewolf role.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Villager 1: Nobody has information yet, so I propose we not vote anyone out on day one.
Turn 2 — Werewolf A (posing as villager): Agreeing with Villager 1 — but I noticed Villager 3 stayed silent, which reads as evasive.
Turn 3 — Villager 3: I was silent because there was nothing to say. Pointing at silence on day one is exactly what a wolf does.
Turn 4 — Seer: I have information I would rather not reveal yet. I will say only that Villager 3's defense is consistent with what I saw.
Turn 5 — Werewolf B: Then reveal it, or the claim is worthless. Voting Villager 3.
Turn 6 — Villager 1: Werewolf B pushing hard right after A pointed the same direction is the strongest signal so far. Voting Werewolf B.
Turn 7 — Villager 3: Agreed, voting Werewolf B.
Turn 8 — Moderator: Werewolf B eliminated. Night falls.

steps.content: Proposed not voting anyone out on day one for lack of information.
Posed as a villager, agreed, then cast suspicion on Villager 3 for staying silent.
Defended the silence and named the accusation itself as wolf-like behavior.
Withheld the specific claim but publicly endorsed Villager 3's consistency.
Demanded the Seer reveal or be ignored, and voted Villager 3.
Identified the coordinated push from A and B as the strongest signal and voted Werewolf B.
Joined the vote against Werewolf B.
Eliminated Werewolf B and advanced to night.

task: Produce a reproducibility checklist for a submitted paper by dividing the manuscript among reviewers.
transcript:
Turn 1 — Lead: Splitting the manuscript: Reviewer A takes data and preprocessing, Reviewer B takes model and training, Reviewer C takes evaluation. Report gaps only.
Turn 2 — Reviewer A: Dataset is named but the split seed is unreported, and the filtering threshold appears only in a figure caption.
Turn 3 — Reviewer B: Hyperparameters are complete; compute budget and hardware are missing entirely.
Turn 4 — Reviewer C: Metric definitions are precise, but significance testing is described as "standard" without naming a test.
Turn 5 — Lead: Compiling four gaps. Reviewer B, does the appendix mention hardware anywhere?
Turn 6 — Reviewer B: Checked — no hardware mention in appendix either. Confirmed as a genuine gap.
Turn 7 — Lead: Checklist finalized with four required author responses.

steps.content: Divided the manuscript across three reviewers by section and asked for gaps only.
Reported an unreported split seed and a filtering threshold buried in a figure caption.
Reported complete hyperparameters but missing compute budget and hardware.
Reported precise metrics but unnamed significance testing.
Compiled the gaps and asked Reviewer B to double-check the appendix for hardware.
Confirmed no hardware mention in the appendix either.
Finalized the checklist with four required author responses.
